body.x: Griffin Technology(www.griffintechnology.com), creator of award-winning and thoughtfully designed mobile accessories, unveiled LightRunner, Tracker Clip and other popular accessories for wearables and armband collection at CES Unveiled, a pre-show of CES 2015 which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

LightRunner is an extremely comfortable neoprene smartphone armband that allows users to jog safely at night with its embedded LED lights for higher visibility. The armband’s touch-through window gives unhindered access to the smartphone’s touchscreen and built-in fingerprint scanners. LightRunner fits iPhone 6, Galaxy S5 and other smartphones up to 4.7". Its adjustable velcro closure adjusts to arms up to 18” wide.

Griffin's fitness lineup also includes new additions to its accessories for wearables collection. As the first accessory manufacturer to create accessories for wearables, Griffin has continued to offer comfortable and convenient ways to wear fitness trackers since the introduction of the category in early 2014. The new CES lineup adds functional yet attractive options to help people show off their fitness trackers.

Tracker Clip allows users to keep track of their activity whether at the gym, the office, or a night out all while looking outfit-appropriate. The sleek Tracker Clip features a manganese alloy clip that slides securely onto clothing, letting users keep their Fitbit discreetly on them at all times. The micro-mesh upper layer allows the Fitbit’s display to show through. Tracker Clip will be available Spring 2015.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
